title: Emergency decisions made on a video call must be written back into the secure channel afterwards
content:
A.1.10.5.2.3.1 permits the Core Facilitator to communicate the decision to use a Standby Spell either in the secure private channel "or on a 'war room' video call" — but then adds that once "the decision to use a Standby Spell is first reached on a video call, the Core Facilitator is required thereafter to promptly document their decision" in that channel. A.1.10.5.3.2.1 repeats the requirement verbatim for Protego, and A.1.10.5.2.3.2.2 applies the same logic to Custom Spell Voting, whose expert recommendation "must be explicitly documented" in the channel.

The distinction being drawn is between the venue where a decision is *made* and the medium in which it *exists*. Synchronous voice is the fastest way to converge in a crisis; it is also unsearchable, unattributable after the fact, and invisible to anyone who was not on the call.

The requirement is load-bearing rather than bureaucratic, because downstream obligations depend on the written artifact. A.1.10.5.2.3.3 bars ADs from voting until they have *received* the announcement of the decision, and A.1.10.5.2.3.2 requires Core GovOps to acknowledge receipt in the same channel. An undocumented war-room decision therefore cannot legally progress — no delegate can satisfy their precondition.

The generalizable rule: allow fast informal coordination, but require a written trace before any authority derived from that decision can be exercised.
description: War-room calls are allowed as the venue for reaching a decision but not as its record; the Core Facilitator must promptly document it in the Emergency Response Signal Group.
